claim: 9B TP16 BRING-UP: first infrastructure wall fixed, second characterized. The bridge admission budget (8 regular + 8 excess client connections per host GPU bridge) covered only eight ranks' scheduler-plus-auxiliary connections; ranks past that had ROCr init silently rejected, dying with 'No CUDA GPUs are available' (first lane: rank 10). Fix: budgets raised to 64+64 (zcode/gem5-absorb 20a2ceaa1) with the TP16 arithmetic documented. After the raise, the second lane's first-failure rank moved from 10 to 13 and all nineteen simulator sessions completed the bridge handshake -- the budget was a real wall of several. The remaining failure mode: a late rank's torch still reports no devices during scheduler init, pointing at a session-endpoint discovery race or a per-rank ROCr init timeout under sixteen-way concurrent spawn (19 sessions, host 44GB free, no OOM entries). Next: instrument the runtime's session selection for the failing rank, consider staggering scheduler spawn, and lengthen the 15 s handshake timeout; the capsule-first methodology applies once a lane gets past weight load.
